key_insight: Only constraints that remain valid after coarse-graining should be enforced exactly; for filtered turbulence data, linear conservation laws survive, while nonlinear PDE residuals can impose the wrong closure.
engineering_relevance: A cheap Fourier-space projection can enforce continuity and momentum balance in neural-operator rollouts with far better stability than plain or physics-informed losses, making it a practical tool for turbulent flow emulation.
method: Use a Fourier neural operator as the base surrogate for 2D incompressible turbulence.
Apply a closed-form projection to enforce continuity and global momentum balance exactly at O(N log N) cost.
Optionally close nonlinear energy balance with a learned constant subgrid flux fitted from coarse data.
evidence_signal: On truncated isotropic turbulence, the projection reduced continuity error to 5.0e-7 and momentum-balance error to 8.6e-11, and increased bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on Kolmogorov flow it was about 3,300× cheaper per trajectory than test-time optimization.
watch_item: Exact enforcement is only safe for constraints that survive filtering; nonlinear laws require an explicit closure model, otherwise the physics loss can encode biased subgrid behavior.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
